parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: The mass of a spherical comet of radius $3.6\text{ km}$ is approximately $1.0 \times 10^{13}\text{ kg}$.
parts.text: Assuming that the comet has constant density, calculate the gravitational field strength on the surface of the comet.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: A probe having a weight of $960\text{ N}$ on Earth lands on the comet. Using your answer in (i), determine the weight of the probe on the surface of the comet.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A second comet has a length of approximately $4.5\text{ km}$ and a width of approximately $2.6\text{ km}$. Its outline is illustrated in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1}}

Fig. 1.1

Suggest one similarity and one difference between the gravitational fields at the surface of this comet and at the surface of the comet in (b).
